arxiv-2203-04992.title: Effective drag in rotating, poorly conducting plasma turbulence Geophysical High-Order Suite for Turbulence (GHOST). Branch: pre-release-2, Commit: 979b9fee3425dd7836687ffe6acff66e41d7083f ( Benavides 2021 ) . Forked and modified from Mininni et al. 2011 , see https://github.com/pmininni/GHOST .
arxiv-2203-04992.creator: Santiago J. Benavides, Keaton J. Burns, Basile Gallet, Glenn R. Flierl
arxiv-2203-04992.description: Abstract Despite the increasing sophistication of numerical models of hot Jupiter atmospheres, the large time-scale separation required in simulating the wide range in electrical conductivity between the dayside and nightside has made it difficult to run fully consistent magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) models. This has led to many studies that resort to drag parametrizations of MHD.

arxiv-2205-11686.title: On Advances in Text Generation from Images Beyond Captioning: A Case Study in Self-Rationalization
arxiv-2205-11686.creator: Shruti Palaskar †♣∗ Akshita Bhagia ‡ Yonatan Bisk † Florian Metze † Alan W Black † Ana Marasović §∗ † Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA, USA ‡ Allen Institute for AI, Seattle, WA, USA § University of Utah, Salt Lake City, UT, USA {spalaska,ybisk,fmetze,awb}@cs.cmu.edu akshitab@allenai.org a
arxiv-2205-11686.description: Abstract Combining the visual modality with pretrained language models has been surprisingly effective for simple descriptive tasks such as image captioning. More general text generation however remains elusive. We take a step back and ask: How do these models work for more complex generative tasks, i.e. conditioning on both text and images?

arxiv-2312-03073.title: Universality in driven open quantum matter
arxiv-2312-03073.creator: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, Sebastian Diehl
arxiv-2312-03073.description: Abstract Universality is a powerful concept, which enables making qualitative and quantitative predictions in systems with extensively many degrees of freedom. It finds realizations in almost all branches of physics, including in the realm of nonequilibrium systems. Our focus here is on its manifestations within a specific class of nonequilibrium stationary states: driven open quantum matter.

arxiv-2406-01152.title: Learning-based legged locomotion; state of the art and future perspectives
arxiv-2406-01152.creator: Sehoon Ha \affilnum 1, Joonho Lee \affilnum 2, Michiel van de Panne \affilnum 3, Zhaoming Xie \affilnum 4, Wenhao Yu \affilnum 5, Majid Khadiv \affilnum 6
arxiv-2406-01152.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sehoon Ha \affilnum 1, Joonho Lee \affilnum 2, Michiel van de Panne \affilnum 3, Zhaoming Xie \affilnum 4, Wenhao Yu \affilnum 5, Majid Khadiv \affilnum 6. Legged locomotion holds the premise of universal mobility, a critical capability for many real-world robotic applications. Both model-based and learning-based approaches have advanced the field of legged locomotion in the past three decades.

arxiv-2408-11678.title: Improved Blow-Up Criterion in a Variational Framework for Nonlinear SPDEs
arxiv-2408-11678.creator: Daniel Goodair
arxiv-2408-11678.description: Abstract We extend recent existence and uniqueness results for maximal solutions of SPDEs through an improved blow-up criterion. Whilst the maximal time of existence is typically characterised by blow-up in the energy norm of solutions, we show instead that solutions exist until blow-up in the larger spaces of the variational framework.

arxiv-2410-06343.title: Losing Treewidth In The Presence Of Weights
arxiv-2410-06343.creator: Michał Włodarczyk
arxiv-2410-06343.description: Abstract In the Weighted Treewidth- η \eta Deletion problem we are given a node-weighted graph G G and we look for a vertex subset X X of minimum weight such that the treewidth of G − X G-X is at most η \eta .

arxiv-2410-10191.title: Bounding ε \varepsilon -scatter dimension via metric sparsity Thanks: Marcin is supported by Polish National Science Centre SONATA BIS-12 grant number 2022/46/E/ST6/00143.
arxiv-2410-10191.creator: Romain Bourneuf, Marcin Pilipczuk
arxiv-2410-10191.description: Abstract A recent work of Abbasi et al. [FOCS 2023] introduced the notion of ε \varepsilon -scatter dimension of a metric space and showed a general framework for efficient parameterized approximation schemes (so-called EPASes) for a wide range of clustering problems in classes of metric spaces that admit a bound on the ε \varepsilon -scatter dimension.

arxiv-2501-00229.title: Relative entropy formulation of thermalization process in a Schwarzschild spacetime
arxiv-2501-00229.creator: Si-Wei Han, Zhichun Ouyang, Zhiyao Hu, Jun Feng
arxiv-2501-00229.description: Abstract We revisit the problem of the thermalization process in an entropic formulation for the Unruh-DeWitt (UDW) detector outside a Schwarzschild black hole. We derive the late-time dynamics of the detector in the context of open quantum system, and capture the path distinguishability and thermodynamic irreversibility of detector thermalization process by using quantum relative entropy (QRE).

arxiv-2503-18572.title: Identifying and Characterising Higher Order Interactions in Mobility Networks Using Hypergraphs
arxiv-2503-18572.creator: Prathyush Sambaturu, Bernardo Gutierrez, Moritz U.G. Kraemer
arxiv-2503-18572.description: Abstract . Understanding human mobility is essential for applications ranging from urban planning to public health. Traditional mobility models such as flow networks and colocation matrices capture only pairwise interactions between discrete locations, overlooking higher-order relationships among locations (i.e., mobility flow among two or more locations).

arxiv-2503-22155.title: Characterizing CJPL’s Site-Specific Neutrino Floor as the Neutrino Fog Boundary
arxiv-2503-22155.creator: Yingjie Fan, Xuewen Liu, Ning Zhou
arxiv-2503-22155.description: Abstract The neutrino floor, a theoretical sensitivity limit for Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) in direct dark matter (DM) detection experiments, is redefined as the boundary of a dynamic “neutrino fog”, where neutrino signals become inevitable, obscuring DM detection due to the statistical and systematic uncertainties.

arxiv-2512-07220.title: Local Reversibility and Divergent Markov Length in 1+1-D Directed Percolation
arxiv-2512-07220.creator: Yu-Hsueh Chen, Tarun Grover
arxiv-2512-07220.description: Abstract Recent progress in open many-body quantum systems has highlighted the importance of the Markov length, the characteristic scale over which conditional correlations decay. It has been proposed that non-equilibrium phases of matter can be defined as equivalence classes of states connected by short-time evolution while maintaining a finite Markov length, a notion called local reversibility.

pmc-11496821.description: This study was conducted with the objective of evaluating the impact of replacing inorganic mineral sources (IM) with amino acid complexed minerals (AACM) in laying hens’ diets on performance, egg quality, bone, and intestinal health. The effects of 4 different diets with varying levels of AACM substitution were evaluated on 400 Lohmann White hens aged 78–98 weeks.

pmc-12428892.creator: Yoshinori Tanino, Xintao Wang, Takefumi Nikaido, Yuki Sato, Ryuichi Togawa, Natsumi Watanabe, Mishie Tanino, Kenji Kadomatsu, Yoko Shibata

It also plays important roles in several inflammatory diseases such as sepsis. However, the role of MDK in the lungs has not yet been elucidated.

pmc-12617597.title: Smoking cessation in India: A narrative review
pmc-12617597.creator: Anubhuti Singh, Kislay Kishore
pmc-12617597.description: Tobacco is the leading preventable cause of death in the world, and India is the second largest consumer of tobacco. Smoking is associated with a myriad of respiratory diseases, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, pneumonia, and lung cancer. Smoking cessation is the only modality which has shown to reduce lung function decline.

pmc-13103307.title: DPEP2 suppresses hyperinflammation via metabolic reprogramming of macrophages in sepsis
pmc-13103307.creator: Wenchen Luo, Wei Xu, Qimeng Yin, Jieqiong Song, Jie Wang, Yian Guan, Jian Huang, Jian Yu, Kefeng Zou, Danfeng Jin, Chao Xu, Min Qiu, Zhixin Qiu, Jing Zhong
pmc-13103307.description: Sepsis-induced excessive inflammation contributes to mortality, but restricting hyperinflammation in sepsis remains challenging. Here, we identify dipeptidase 2 (DPEP2) as an immunotherapeutic target in sepsis by integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data from septic patients. In patients with sepsis, peripheral monocytes/macrophages have reduced DPEP2 expression, with DPEP2 levels negatively correlating with inflammation severity, disease progression, and clinical outcomes.

pmc-13379586.title: A nucleolar stress gene signature enables quantitative scoring across multi-omics contexts
pmc-13379586.creator: Jianxiong Chen, Shuai Xiao, Zhe Hao, Huimeng Xu, Xuemei Xu, Jun Zhou
pmc-13379586.description: The nucleolus is essential for ribosome biogenesis and cellular homeostasis, and its dysfunction can induce nucleolar stress, a process implicated in cancer and other diseases. However, nucleolar stress is commonly inferred from morphological changes or a limited set of functional assays, and quantitative approaches based on gene expression profiles remain lacking.

pmc-13381772.title: Genomic insights into the medieval cultivation history of influential high-yielding Asian rice
pmc-13381772.creator: Ngoc Hai Trieu Phong, Yoshihiro Kawahara, Masahiko Kumagai, Takeshi Itoh
pmc-13381772.description: High-yielding rice landraces that contributed substantially to historical population expansions were widely cultivated across Asia. These landraces are generally believed to have been Champa rice, which originated in present-day Vietnam. Historical records indicate that Champa rice was disseminated to southern China in the eleventh century and subsequently transmitted to medieval western Japan.

pmc-13459901.title: Camelina seeds and their glucosinolate, glucocamelinin, counteract severe fatty liver in rodents with monogenic obesity

pmc-13459901.description: BackgroundObesity is associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), for which drugs and nutraceuticals are being developed. We investigated whether camelina seeds from the Brassicaceae family and their components can attenuate metabolic disorders in animal models of genetic obesity, including fatty liver.MethodsIn two separate 5-week experiments, female obese (fa/fa) Zucker rats and female db/db mice were used.

pmc-13535247.creator: Andrea de Ruvo, Pierluigi Castelli, Andrea Bucciacchio, Iolanda Mangone, Verónica Mixão, Vítor Borges, Michele Flammini, Nicolas Radomski, Adriano Di Pasquale
pmc-13535247.description: Bacterial genomic surveillance requires balancing computational efficiency with genetic resolution for effective cluster investigation. cgMLST distance calculations treat all allelic differences as equivalent units, obscuring nucleotide-level variation. Furthermore, single nucleotide polymorphism-based pipelines provide finer resolution at substantially higher computational cost, which limits their routine deployment in surveillance laboratories.
